newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps steady, slightly down in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps steady, slightly down in slow trade.

text.p: European oil swaps were a touch easier on Friday in a very slow market with the U.S. out of the running and European traders enjoying a breather ahead of the weekend.
CFDs and gasoline swaps were slightly easier after crude's selloff yesterday, but fuel and naphtha were unchanged.
"There is very little going on," said one dealer.

Brent CFDs were a couple of cents off with July 7-11 slipping to flat against August Brent compared with +4 cents on Thursday while July 14-18 was hovering around -13 cents against August from -11/12 cents. July 21-25 was steady at -15/16 cents as was July 28-August 1 at -19 cents.
Heavy fuel was pegged at $84.00 for July with August $1 contangoed and September a further $1.50 stronger. Wet barges traded at $84 and $85 fob, but business was slow.

Gasoline swaps eased off $1 or so with July slipping to $186.50 and August sliding to $185.50. Traders said the drop reflected crude's drop yesterday and its inability to reverse the falls on Friday morning.
Naphtha was particularly slow with swaps levels steady, but showing signs of bearish pressure.
